chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from his grandfather Abi al-Bilad, raising it (to the Prophet), said:

A Bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he was intending for one of his military expeditions, so he grabbed the reins of his riding animal and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed by which I may enter Paradise.' He said, 'Whatever you love that people should come to you with, go to them with it, and whatever you dislike that people should come to you with, do not go to them with it.' He freed the way of the riding animal.
ai.seo_question: What is the fundamental ethical principle taught by the Prophet for entering Paradise?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) distills the essence of Islamic ethics into the 'Golden Rule,' emphasizing reciprocal justice as the key to Paradise. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for deriving universal moral principles from specific interactions, linking personal conduct directly to spiritual salvation. The immediate instruction to release the camel underscores the practical application of this ethic, where spiritual teaching is accompanied by tangible, gentle action.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad bin Abu Abdullah, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from his grandfather Abu Al Balaad, raising it,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A Bedouin came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he<sup>saww</sup> wanted (to go on to) one of his<sup>saww</sup> military expeditions. So he grabbed one of the reins of his<sup>saww</sup> riding animal, and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Teach me a deed by which I can enter the Paradise’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whatever you love the people to come to you with, so go to them with it, and whatever you dislike the people coming to you with, so do not go to them with it’. He freed the way of the riding animal’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn abu al-Bilad from his father from his grandfather, abu al- Bilad in a marfu’ manner saying:

“Once an Arab man came to the Holy Prophet when he was about to leave for an armed campaign. The Arab held on to the harness of the horse of the Holy Prophet and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed with which I can go to paradise.’ He said, ‘Do to people what you like them to do to you, and do not do anything to people that you do not like to be done to you. Now allow the horse to go.’”
